title: Early peak lactate and clinical outcomes
summary: Design coordinates for descriptive or prognostic associations using peak lactate in a prespecified early ICU window. Peak values are affected by the observation window, assay harmonization, clinical measurement intensity, and early outcomes; the analysis must distinguish an association from a causal effect and must retain the measured-versus-unmeasured denominator.

design_candidates.population: A locked ICU cohort with an explicit hospital-outcome denominator; retain all eligible stays for the lactate-measured versus unmeasured comparison and define the lactate-measured analysis subset separately.
design_candidates.time_zero: A prespecified clinical anchor such as ICU admission; do not choose the anchor after inspecting lactate or outcome values.
design_candidates.observation_window: A fixed early window anchored to time zero; include only lactate values whose timestamps and units are verified and exclude values recorded after death or discharge.
design_candidates.prediction_or_followup_window: For a descriptive in-hospital association, state that exposure ascertainment and outcome time may overlap; for prospective or time-to-event claims, start follow-up after the exposure window or use a correctly specified time-varying analysis.
eligibility_candidates: Do not require repeated lactate measurements when the prespecified exposure is a peak; one verified in-window value is sufficient
Preserve measured, unmeasured, and source-missing states; never encode unmeasured lactate as zero
Report specimen, assay, and units or document the harmonization contract
design_candidates.exposure: Maximum verified lactate within the locked early window, reported in harmonized units with its skewed distribution and prespecified continuous or categorical representation.
design_candidates.outcome: A clearly defined hospital or time-bounded mortality outcome with the denominator and event horizon reported.
design_candidates.estimand: A descriptive adjusted association between early peak lactate and the declared outcome among the stated analysis population; do not label it a causal effect.
recommended_methods: Report the full-cohort lactate measurement rate and compare measured versus unmeasured patients before modelling
Report median and interquartile range for skewed lactate and estimate a continuous association with uncertainty; assess nonlinearity rather than assuming one linear unit effect
Choose covariates using prespecified baseline roles and keep post-exposure treatment variables out of a primary descriptive adjustment unless their role is explicitly justified
sensitivity_analyses: Alternative prespecified early windows and initial versus peak lactate when both are available
Restriction to patients alive and under observation at the end of the exposure window when a post-window estimand is claimed
Quantify selection by lactate measurement status or sampling intensity rather than treating observed measurements as random

stop_conditions: Lactate timestamps, units, or the early-window anchor cannot be verified
Measured, unmeasured, and source-missing lactate states cannot be distinguished
A prospective or causal conclusion is requested but the exposure window overlaps outcome follow-up without a valid temporal strategy
requires_confirmation: Confirm the time-zero anchor, early-window duration, and whether initial or peak lactate is primary
Confirm that the target is descriptive association, prognosis, or a causal question; these require different estimands
